rv.q: It’s an impressive piece of solo performance, and, whenever you go, you’re guaranteed to get something you didn’t expect.
But the flaw in his soft-liberal approach, which implies a moral equivalence between all forms of protest, is that it comes dangerously close to Trumpism...
It’s all suitably entertaining, for sure, but I’m not sure it sparks as much debate as it could.

The Majority is a provocative one man show originally produced at the Arches Theatre in Glasgow. Writer performer Rob Drummond was approached to create a piece on the Scottish Independence referendum. As a pessimist he was disinterested in politics and struggled to find a human interest angle until he met a man who was selling his vote on e-bay.

cn.t: Rob Drummond's interactive show uses audience voting to explore ethical dilemmas and political questions, earning praise for its timeliness and nuanced approach, though some critics question its binary choices.
